preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and x >= 1 for x in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) and all(0 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The first line of stdin is T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10^5), followed by T lines each containing two integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5, 0 ≤ k ≤ n).

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 1 and line.strip() == '-1' or (len(line.split()) == n and all(1 <= int(x) <= n and x != y for x, y in zip(line.split(), range(1, n + 1))) and sum(1 for i in range(1, n + 1) if int(line.split()[i - 1]) == i) == k) for line, n, k in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]], [int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) if line.strip() != '-1')
postconditions.description: For each test case, if no valid permutation exists, stdout contains '-1'. Otherwise, stdout contains a permutation of 1..n where exactly k indices i satisfy A_i = i. The permutation is a space-separated list of integers, and each integer from 1 to n appears exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(line.strip() == '-1' or (k <= n and k >= max(0, n - (n - k)) and k >= 0) for line, n, k in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]], [int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) if line.strip() != '-1')
postconditions.description: A valid permutation exists if and only if k is between 0 and n, and k ≥ n - (n - k) (i.e., k ≥ 0 and k ≤ n, and the number of fixed points k is feasible given the constraints of permutation construction).
